We need to determine number of CH3 groups in the sample's compound. We have no direct description of the sample. We need to infer from NMR data perhaps. We can request proton NMR spectra (which will show methyl signals). Or carbon NMR to see methyl carbons. Use minimal experiments. Probably easiest: get proton NMR and count methyl peaks (triplet etc). But we need to know number of CH3 groups, not just peaks (could be overlapping). Could also use carbon NMR to count distinct methyl carbon signals. But we don't know the structure.

We have no SMILES. So we need to measure NMR. Use proton_nmr_spectra tool (no args). It will return a string with peaks. Then we can parse for methyl signals (around 0.9 ppm, singlet, doublet, etc). But we need to count number of CH3 groups, not just signals. If overlapping, ambiguous. Could also get carbon NMR to see signals around 10-30 ppm for methyl carbons. That may give count of distinct methyl carbons. Might be enough.

Let's first get proton NMR.
